log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: Mirror match: the opponent has the same six. I plan to bring Garchomp (mega), Gholdengo and Kingambit. Dragapult has a Choice Scarf and outspeeds nearly everything. Garchomp should lead, and Gholdengo handles Kingambit and Garchomp.

Mirror match. Mega Garchomp now with Dragon Claw, which is super effective on their Garchomp. Gholdengo is weak to Ground, so keep it away from Garchomp's Earthquake. Dragapult (Choice Scarf) outspeeds nearly everything.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm thinking about the mirror matchup between the two Garchomp, both likely holding Garchompite. Mega Garchomp's base speed drops to 92, so its speed stat will actually be lower than the non-mega 169 figure I'm seeing, which matters for determining who moves first.

Gholdengo is a poor switch-in since Steel/Ghost is weak to Ground. Best plan is just to mega evolve and fire off Dragon Claw for solid super-effective damage, since both sides mega'ing would lower their speed roughly equally anyway.

decisions.thought: Mirror match. My Garchomp (35 HP) moved first on turn 1, so I likely outspeed. Dragon Claw should finish their Garchomp at 18%. Keep Gholdengo away from Ground moves. Their Dragapult has a Choice Scarf. Gholdengo and Kingambit are my backups.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Our Garchomp went first on turn 1, so we likely outspeed the opponent's mega or at worst tied. With the opponent at 18% HP, either Dragon Claw or Earthquake should finish them off this turn.

decisions.thought: Opponent's Garchomp (mega, 18% HP) has Earthquake and Dragon Claw. Switching in Kingambit to Sucker Punch it, because it survives Earthquake more often than Gholdengo does. Opponent still has 2 of: kingambit, gholdengo, incineroar, corviknight, dragapult. Dragapult has a Choice Scarf.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Garchomp fainted while the opponent's mega Garchomp is left at 18%. I'm trying to work out the turn order — it seems like they got an Earthquake in before I could act on turn 2, even though I thought I moved first on turn 1, so I'm puzzling over the speed/priority here.

Now I'm weighing whether Kingambit or Gholdengo is the better switch-in against their weakened Garchomp. Sucker Punch would kill it at 18% HP if Kingambit moves first, but I need to check if Garchomp's Earthquake would do too much damage to Kingambit on the switch given its Steel typing weakness, while Gholdengo resists less favorably against Ground but may have a speed edge. I'm running the math on Earthquake's damage against Kingambit's bulk to see if it survives the hit before countering.

decisions.thought: Opponent Garchomp (mega, 18% HP) has Earthquake and Dragon Claw. Sucker Punch should KO it before it moves, if it attacks. Opponent still has 2 of: kingambit, gholdengo, incineroar, corviknight, dragapult. Dragapult holds a Choice Scarf. Gholdengo is weak to Ground.

Opponent has Incineroar out and one more to come (kingambit, gholdengo, corviknight or dragapult). Dragapult holds a Choice Scarf. Incineroar resists both my Dark and Steel moves, and its Fire moves hit Kingambit and Gholdengo hard. Plan: Swordsdance with Kingambit to undo the Intimidate drop, then hit hard. Gholdengo is weak to Ground and Fire.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking the matchup between Kingambit and Incineroar, weighing how Fire is super effective against Kingambit's Steel typing while Incineroar resists both Dark and Steel-type moves.

Gholdengo faces a similar problem since it's weak to Fire, though its Ghost typing lets it resist Dark somewhat. Overall Kingambit seems to be at a disadvantage here, likely taking heavy damage from Flare Blitz while struggling to deal much back with Kowtow Cleave or Sucker Punch.

Flare Blitz would deal roughly 72% to Kingambit, leaving it dangerously low with recoil hurting Incineroar too. Swords Dance seems too risky since a follow-up hit plus Sucker Punch wouldn't finish things off reliably, so switching Gholdengo in to eat the Flare Blitz and threaten back with Shadow Ball looks like the safer option.

decisions.thought: Turn 5: Kingambit has 39 HP and Atk +1, and Incineroar (72%) outspeeds it. Using Sucker Punch to chip it before Kingambit likely dies. Gholdengo then comes in, but both its Steel and Ghost moves are resisted by Incineroar, and Fire is a threat to it. Opponent's last Pokémon is one of kingambit, gholdengo, corviknight or dragapult. Dragapult holds a Choice Scarf.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Kingambit is at 39 HP with an attack boost, but Incineroar outspeeds and likely KOs it with any hit, and Flare Blitz would also threaten Gholdengo since it's super effective on steel. Gholdengo's Good as Gold at least blocks status so Intimidate isn't a concern here.

Checking Gholdengo's options: Shadow Ball is resisted by Dark, and Make It Rain is resisted by both Fire and Dark, so neither move hits hard. For Kingambit, Sucker Punch is also resisted, but its priority means it could strike first if Incineroar attacks — running the damage math, it lands around 70-85 damage against Incineroar's roughly 137 remaining HP, not quite enough for a KO on its own.

Incineroar could also just switch out or use Parting Shot/U-turn instead of attacking, but Sucker Punch is still the safest option here. If it doesn't move first, Kingambit is going down anyway without acting, so Sucker Punch is the call.

decisions.note: Only one legal action: played without asking.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo is my last Pokémon. Incineroar (50%) resists both of my attacks and Flare Blitz is super effective on Gholdengo. Use Make It Rain to bring it low so recoil or a follow-up finishes it. The opponent's last Pokémon is one of kingambit, gholdengo, corviknight or dragapult. Dragapult holds a Choice Scarf.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm working out whether Incineroar's Flare Blitz would be super effective enough against Gholdengo's Steel typing to score a knockout, cross-checking against the damage Kingambit took earlier to estimate the rough power level needed.

I'm also considering alternatives like Make It Rain or Shadow Ball, checking their type effectiveness against Incineroar's Fire/Dark typing and whether the resisted damage would be enough to finish it off at 50% HP.

Either way Gholdengo likely goes down to Flare Blitz next turn regardless of choice, so the priority is dealing maximum damage now and hoping the recoil from Flare Blitz finishes Incineroar off afterward.

Since this is my last Pokémon, I either win or lose this exchange outright. Going with Make It Rain now — if Incineroar is slower and I survive its Flare Blitz, I win; if it's faster, I was losing regardless.
